question: Why is female genital mutilation (FGM) traditionally performed?

options.A: To prevent severe pelvic infections in young girls
options.B: To enhance natural hormonal balance during puberty
options.D: To comply with non-medical cultural and social beliefs

explanation: Spot on! FGM is done for cultural or social reasons, not for any medical treatment or health benefit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h1)

question: How do global health organizations view female genital mutilation?

options.A: As an acceptable traditional surgical option
options.B: As a violation of basic human rights
options.C: As a mandatory rite of passage for health
options.D: As a minor procedure with minimal complications

explanation: Correct! Major health bodies view FGM as a serious violation of human rights and bodily safety for women and girls. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h1)

question: Into how many main categories does the World Health Organization divide FGM?
explanation: You got it! The WHO classifies FGM into four broad types based on the method and extent of tissue removed. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h2)

question: Why do nurses and doctors use a standard classification system for FGM?

options.A: To help healthcare workers document and assess clinical needs
options.B: To assign legal penalties to specific practitioners
options.C: To determine the correct surgical reversal technique
options.D: To calculate the financial cost of hospital treatment

explanation: Exactly! Knowing the specific type helps nurses understand the patient's history and plan the best, most sensitive care possible. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h2)

question: Which body part is mainly affected in Type I FGM?
explanation: Spot on! Type I involves removing part or all of the clitoris and its surrounding skin fold (the prepuce). You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is a common long-term effect specifically linked to removing the clitoris?

options.A: Permanent closure of the vaginal canal
options.B: Complete paralysis of the lower extremities
options.C: Chronic loss of sensory and sexual function
options.D: Continuous production of excess amniotic fluid

explanation: Correct! Because the clitoris has many sensitive nerve endings, removing it leads to lasting sensory changes and distress. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h3)

question: How is Type II FGM different from Type I?

options.A: It also includes removal of the labia minora
options.B: It leaves the clitoris completely untouched
options.C: It only involves stitching the vaginal opening shut
options.D: It is performed exclusively using modern surgical lasers

explanation: You nailed it! Type II goes a step further than Type I by also removing the inner labia (labia minora), and sometimes the outer labia too. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h4)

question: During a pelvic exam, what physical sign would you expect in a patient with Type II FGM?

options.A: A completely sealed vaginal opening with a tiny pinhole
options.B: An intact hymen with no external scars
options.C: Extensive scar tissue and absence of the labia minora

explanation: Well done! The removal of both the clitoris and labia minora leaves clear signs of scar tissue and missing external structures. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the main feature of Type III FGM?

options.A: Removal of only the clitoral prepuce
options.B: Piercing of the labia majora with metal rings
options.C: Creation of a covering seal that narrows the vaginal opening
options.D: Cauterization of the inner vaginal lining with heat

explanation: Correct! Type III (infibulation) involves cutting and joining the labia to form a seal, leaving only a very small opening for urine and menstrual flow. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h5)

question: Why might a woman with Type III FGM need a procedure called defibulation during childbirth?

options.A: To prevent severe postpartum hemorrhage from the uterus
options.B: To allow the baby to pass through the narrowed vaginal opening
options.C: To correct an underlying urinary tract infection
options.D: To speed up the delivery of the placenta

explanation: Spot on! The scar tissue seal blocks the birth canal, so healthcare providers must surgically open the area during labor to keep mother and baby safe. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h5)

question: Which of these practices falls under Type IV FGM?

options.A: Surgical repair of a relaxed pelvic floor
options.B: Complete surgical removal of the uterus
options.C: Piercing or scraping of the female genitalia
options.D: Routine episiotomy performed during hospital delivery

explanation: You got it! Type IV covers other harmful practices like piercing, scraping, or burning the external genitalia without medical cause. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h6)

question: Which statement is true about Type IV FGM?

options.A: It still poses serious risks of bleeding, pain, and infection
options.B: It is always performed by licensed medical doctors
options.C: It is universally recognized as a form of childbirth preparation
options.D: It carries no risk of infection because it is minor

explanation: Correct! Even though Type IV uses different methods like piercing or scraping, any non-medical cutting of genital tissue carries high risks. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h6)

question: What is the most common immediate complication right after an FGM procedure?
explanation: Spot on! Cutting sensitive genital tissue with basic tools typically causes immediate, heavy bleeding and intense pain. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h7)

question: A young woman with a history of FGM comes to the clinic with lower tummy pain and painful urination. What is a likely cause?

options.B: Chronic urinary tract infections from scarring

explanation: You nailed it! Scarring and altered anatomy from FGM can block normal urine flow, making infections and pain much more likely. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to care for an FGM survivor in the clinic?

options.A: Reporting the adult patient to local police immediately
options.B: Inspecting the surgical site without warning the patient
options.C: Refusing to discuss the cultural background of the practice
options.D: Using a trauma-informed and non-judgmental approach

explanation: Great choice! Trauma-informed care builds trust, lowers anxiety, and makes sure the patient feels safe and respected. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h8)

question: What is an important way community health nurses can help prevent FGM?

options.A: Performing mild forms of FGM under hygienic conditions
options.B: Issuing legal certificates permitting traditional circumcisers
options.C: Subsidizing the cost of traditional ceremonies
options.D: Educating local communities about the health risks of FGM

explanation: Spot on! Community health nurses play a huge role in prevention by raising awareness and teaching families about the dangers of FGM. Brilliant work today! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h8)
